items.note: Story 1 gives the Larrow Valley Cooperative Creamery Association, 1889, Gideon Vose as first president, creamery built at Larrow Green 1891 - all bolded elements present.
Article VII stated correctly: paid by the butterfat test of the station where he delivered, not the weight of his milk.
Calls Article VII 'the hinge of the whole matter' but never states that the rule is what made a wrong test cost money (no payment-by-weight counterfactual) anywhere in Section A.

Only Hobart Sill appears, incidentally as a source and as the lender of glassware; Effie Loomis (secretary 1901, minute book) and Wilbur Teague (bookkeeper 1905) are absent from Section A. The officer roster - the item's core - is not recovered.
Selby Vose is never mentioned in Section A. He appears only at B3/B4, and Section A credit does not travel from Sections B-G. (B3/B4 also date him from 1911, a planted error - see deductions.)
The 'station gain' ledger line appears only in the Section C working at C1(a); nothing in Section A.
Ostrey Hollow station, seven miles up the valley, opened 4 May 1896, glassware borrowed from Larrow Green (Sill's outfit) - all present in Story 1.
No description of the method anywhere in Section A: no weighing at intake, no composite sample, no percent read on the test bottle neck, no fixed charge from the pipette.

Invoice of 14 April 1897 and in use from 1 May 1897, both correct, with the planted 1898/1899/1922 dates explicitly rejected. Item bolds three elements with no REQUIRED line, so the core fact carries it; the supplier (Ammon & Sons, Tarnet) is never named, which is a real miss noted here.

Gives six dozen pipettes, twelve dozen bottles, acid measure, hand tester and the correct $77.93 (with $77.39 properly hedged), but the bolded marked capacity 17.6 c.c. is missing - it appears nowhere in the sheet. Two bolded units, one incomplete.
The flatness of the 0.19 shortfall - same in every month and every one of the twenty-six years, the signature of an instrument - is stated only at C1(b), not in Section A.
No mention of the pipette being uncheckable without a burette, or of there being none in the county.

Ansel Keddie, tester at Ostrey Hollow, 29 unbroken seasons, service ending 1925 - the item's own aspect per the key's collision note (the tester's service and its end). The exact dismissal date 30 April 1925 is never given anywhere.

The only mention of the test book is 'wrote it into his test book' inside the 1911 narrative, which is the element earning A3.4. Nothing of this item's own aspect - the columns, one hand for twenty-nine seasons, corrections crossed and initialed - appears. No fact is scored twice inside Section A.
The summary leaf and the 3.61-from-1898 / 1896-at-3.80 step are absent from Section A; 3.61 and 3.80 appear only in Section C.

The 1911 interval: broke 8 May, borrowed measure until 10 July, nine weeks, readings rose and fell back the day the station's glass returned, Keddie's question mark. The bolded 3.80 is missing, but the item bolds five elements with no REQUIRED line, so the core fact carries it; the planted 'six weeks' is avoided.

Section A calls Orra Keddie 'the tester's own wife' and Duncan 'Emmet's nephew', but never states that Ansel married Orra Brant, sister of Emmet Brant, the station's largest patron. The sibling tie is established only at B1/B2, which cannot travel into Section A.
No 1919 circular in Section A (only 'closed for eleven years, until 1919'), and no Keddie statement of 17 March 1925.
Death in 1934, the impounding of the test book, and the county historical rooms are all absent.

Answer 'granddaughter' (1) plus a derivation (1): cites the named, dated self-correction that displaces 'great-niece' - the resolution the key expects - and builds Duncan as Ansel's son via the Orra/Emmet sibling tie, with Ivy as Duncan's daughter. The hedge on the last link does not cost the point; great-niece is explicitly rejected, so no corruption deduction.

Second cousins with the full derivation (1). Abstention item A08 not earned (0): the sheet never raises whether Emmet and Orra were full or half siblings, so it neither declines it nor notes that half siblings are siblings and the answer is unchanged. No definite assertion either way, so no -2.

Gideon Vose named as the father (1). Significance not earned (0): the sheet's stated significance is inherited standing and unchallenged authority. B4 does say Gideon wrote Article VII making the station's test the basis of payment and that his son signed the 1919 circular, but the sheet never draws the point - that the accuser was enforcing his own father's rule, which is what made a fault in the instrument decide every patron's pay - nor the accepted alternative about the Vose Jerseys losing most.

Abstention A01 earned (1): the verdict sentence is 'none the sources establish by blood or marriage', closing with 'whether any personal tie existed beyond that cannot be determined from the sources' - an abstention, no -2. Second point not earned (0): what is established about the kinship question is not stated - no mention of the two narrators asserting a cousinship from talk, the flat denial, or that a family member's denial is not a record. The sheet substitutes the institutional history instead.

Key requires 16.72 / 17.6 = 0.95, i.e. 95 percent of true, short 5 percent, derived from the glassware. The sheet answers 5.25/5.26 percent, derived as 0.19/3.61 from the ledger and the recorded average; it never mentions 16.72 or 17.6 anywhere. Wrong quantity (that is the credited-fat ratio) and the glassware derivation the question asks for is absent. Not the catalogued '5.26 percent of the true fat' error - the denominator is named correctly as the recorded average - so no deduction.
True average 3.80, recorded tests short 0.19 of a point. Exact match.
40,000,000 lb x 0.19 percent = 76,000 lb. Exact match. The 67,000 lb figure is attributed to a 1925 estimate rather than asserted, so no deduction.

Asserts the loss as $19,600 ('the best-attested total') and therefore 19.4 percent - the NT-8 cascade. Key is $19,000 at 25 cents and exactly 20 percent / one fifth. $3,800 is right but both the money and the fraction are required. Corruption deduction applied separately.
Declined. C2 is not an abstention item: 200,000 lb at a recorded 3.42 gives 6,840 lb credited. The sheet reports it could not find any 1910 or largest-patron figure.
Declined. Key: true test 3.60, true fat 7,200 lb, owed 360 lb.
Declined. Key: 360 x $0.24 = $86.40.

deductions.reason: Asserts the planted loss figure of $19,600 as fact at C1(d) ('$19,600 is the best-attested total'), and builds the 19.4 percent fraction on it (F081).

Asserts Selby Vose as Association manager from 1911 as fact, at B3 ('became the Association's manager in 1911') and again at B4 ('managed the Association from 1911'). Key: manager from 1913 (F009); 1911 is a catalogued planted error.
